final_answer.evidence_summary: Fe is feasible and has the lowest computed canonical cost in the full admissible window among the principal low-price/high-activity candidate and the highest-activity candidate. Ru, despite the highest reference atomic activity, is more expensive after full process optimization and would require a 201.2x intrinsic-activity gain to reach Fe parity, far beyond the descriptor-manifold maximum. The lower-activity/higher-price metals are screened by the declared rule relative to Fe. Os was tested in a favorable high-activity process subwindow and remained well above Fe.

chosen_args.why_stop: Stopping status after the final optimization reports S1, S2, and S3 satisfied. Remaining affordable calculations cannot overturn the decision; full Os optimization, exact dominance, model-validity checks, and MC uncertainty are not affordable with 8 CU remaining.

unresolved_decision_risk.main_residual: Os was not globally optimized over the full window; only a targeted favorable-region probe was affordable. The risk that an unprobed Os state beats Fe is assessed low because Os is slightly less active and ~2.65x more expensive than Ru, while full-window Ru already loses to Fe by 6.74 USD/t and the Os probe cost was 27.05 USD/t.
unresolved_decision_risk.model_validity: Fe optimum has Tsep_C=30 at the separator-temperature upper edge; Ru has T_C=450 at the temperature upper edge. Edge/bed/vessel-floor validity checks were unaffordable, leaving small model-edge risk.
unresolved_decision_risk.descriptor_uncertainty: No MC uncertainty run was affordable after mandatory optimization/parity actions; descriptor uncertainty could shift relative activities, but the large Ru parity multiplier makes a Ru-over-Fe reversal through intrinsic activity alone unlikely on the frozen manifold.
